Hi Anna / Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — it was great to see BrightCart's checkout personalization in action. As promised, a short recap and the asks we committed to follow up on related to data handling and subprocessors. I’ve attached a short set of answers we use for similar customers (redwood-privacy-answers-BrightCart.pdf).

Recap / open items from our call:
- PII scope: you mentioned customer billing info and some email addresses should be treated as high-sensitivity. Need confirmation of the full field list.
- Data residency: you asked whether we can guarantee EU-only storage for EU customers (BrightCart has EU merchants).
- Retention & logs: your security team wants retention windows and ability to redact user identifiers from logs.
- Third-party telemetry / analytics: question about whether Redwood sends any customer-identifying data to telemetry vendors (Mixpanel / Datadog traces) and how marketplace provisioning affects that flow.
- Evidence: SOC 2 and subprocessors list for procurement review.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) You send the short PII field list you want protected (billing_email, billing_name, credit_card_token?) — I can slot that into our standard data classification template.
2) We will provide a short one-page answer (SOC2 + subprocessor list + regional options) by EOD Monday.
3) Sergio (cc’d) / Neha can join a 30-minute follow-up on Tuesday with your security team if helpful.

From: Anna Lopez <anna@brightcart.com>

Subject: Re: BrightCart follow-up: data residency and third-party analytics fit

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- PII fields: primary email, billing_email, billing_name, shipping_address, and any payment tokenized IDs (we do not share raw PANs). I’ll send an exported template by end of day.
- Data residency: for EU merchants we require customer data (including embeddings or any derivative user content) to be stored and processed in an EU region — BrightCart is trying to be GDPR-first. Can you confirm if we can pin an account to EU-only?
- Logs/retention: security asks for 90-day application logs by default, with an option to set retention as short as 7 days for sensitive customers. Also need ability to redact or hash email addresses in logs.
- Telemetry/analytics: internal question — does the Redwood runtime ever send PII to third-party analytics/telemetry vendors? For example, if you have telemetry events or request traces that include user IDs, can that be suppressed?
- Marketplace flow: if we onboard via AWS Marketplace, will any customer metadata go to the marketplace or be visible to third parties? Procurement flagged that as a risk.

We’d like to receive the SOC 2 and list of subprocessors and a clear statement on telemetry by end of day Monday so our procurement can advance. Also, a 30-min call Tuesday morning (10am PT) with your security team would work.

Thanks —
Anna Lopez
Director, Platform Operations | BrightCart
anna@brightcart.com | +1 (206) 555-0179

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>

Rachel — thanks for the ping and Anna for the clear asks. Quick answers below (I’ll attach the doc set we normally send).

- EU-only data residency: Yes — we can pin customer accounts to an EU region. We offer per-account region selection at provisioning and can ensure both storage and inference happen in EU-hosted clusters for those accounts. For BrightCart we can propose an EU-only tenant for all EU merchants.

- Retention & logs: We support configurable retention windows at the account level. Default application/log retention is 90 days; we can set a 7-day retention for sensitive accounts. For logs that include request metadata we have a built-in redaction/transform pipeline to hash or drop email fields before they are stored.

- Telemetry/subprocessors: By default our telemetry (usage metrics, traces) is telemetry-id'd and does not include cleartext PII fields. We have two telemetry destinations: internal metrics (Datadog) and an optional analytics pipeline (customer-tenant telemetry to Mixpanel for product teams). We do not send PII to external analytics vendors. For marketplace flows: provisioning events sent to AWS Marketplace include account identifiers (merchant_id) and a provisioning token — not customer emails or PII. No telemetry vendor receives raw customer PII as part of normal provisioning.

- Evidence: attaching SOC 2 Type II summary and our current subprocessor list (subprocessors-redwood-202706.pdf). We’ll also prepare a one-page targeted statement for BrightCart describing these points for procurement.

Attachments: [Attachment: soc2-summary-redwood.pdf], [Attachment: subprocessors-redwood-202706.pdf]

Next steps: I’ll draft the one-pager and share by Monday 12:00pm PDT. Happy to join the 10am PT call Tuesday with Neha.
